13477-watts-1817-1904:
W. Loftus Hare's short life of the painter George Frederic Watts, 1817 to 1904, appears in the Masterpieces in Colour series with eight colour reproductions. The frontispiece, Death Crowning Innocence, shows a child in the lap of winged Death, a silent angel of pity who takes innocence beyond evil's reach.

Hare reads Watts as a stoic moralist and teacher of earthly things, not a mystic weaving hidden doctrines from Greek myths. Each picture teaches plainly and ethically, from portraits of Tennyson in scholastic robes to John L. Motley, American minister and historian of the Dutch Republic. The book suits readers who want a clear guide to Watts's grave, symbolic art.
15345-the-great-events-by-famous-histori:
Edited by Rossiter Johnson, with Charles Horne and John Rudd, this fourth volume of Great Events by Famous Historians tells world history through famous writers. The plan, drawn from scholars of America and Europe, presents great events as complete narratives in master words, with brief specialist introductions, indices, and chronologies. The set claims no sect or party.

Volume four opens with an outline narrative by Horne, then Gibbon on Visigoths pillaging Rome in 410 and Huns invading the Eastern empire. Attila dictating peace in 441 follows. History readers will find the volume a rich, readable sampler of classic historical writing.
20751-priestley-in-america-1794-1804:
Edgar F. Smith wrote Priestley in America, 1794-1804, on the famed chemist's last decade. Joseph Priestley, driven from England, sparked fresh chemical work in the young republic. Robert Hare and a new breed of American chemists felt his push at once.

Smith asks what Priestley himself did in those years and why it counts. Letters, labs, and church fights fill the account. Priestley had found oxygen and held bold views on faith and rule. His American years join science and exile in one tale. The book suits readers of early American science and of free thought alike.
2104-history-of-friedrich-ii-of-prussia-:
Carlyle turns in this volume to Frederick's apprenticeship as a boy and young prince, from 1713 to 1728, under the hard rule of his father Frederick William. Book Four asks what a childhood at a soldier king's court could teach. Carlyle calls Frederick William a soldier king, and the boy's life under him was drill and fear.

Carlyle admits how little is truly known, and complains of pedantic histories that bury the man in detail. Yet he pieces together the double education, part drill and part books, that shaped the future king's stubborn character. The double education, part court and part camp, left Frederick torn between books and the sword.
3080-original-short-stories-volume-04:
The Moribund opens volume four on a warm autumn farmyard, cows cropping close. Cows crop grass close, rain-soaked earth sinks underfoot with a soggy noise, apple trees drop pale green fruit in dark grass, and four heifers graze in a line. The volume adds The Gamekeeper, The Story of a Farm Girl, The Wreck, Theodule Sabot's Confession, and The Wrong House. The Diamond Necklace, Maupassant's most famous tale, stands at the volume's center, beside The Marquis de Fumerol, The Trip of the Horla, Farewell, The Wolf, and The Inn.

A walk across sands toward a black rock, elastic like flesh and sweating under tread, shows his horror manner. The volume is essential Maupassant, with his greatest hit among quieter masterpieces.
3342-the-wandering-jew-volume-04:
Eugene Sue's serial reaches Book Four, the second part of the chastisement, in this volume. A prologue offers a bird's-eye view of two worlds, as the eagle might see them, before the masquerade, the contrast, and the carouse begin. The farewell, the Florine, and Mother Sainte-Perpetue follow, with the temptation and Mother Bunch beside Mademoiselle de Cardoville.

Encounters, a meeting, and discoveries lead to the penal code and a burglary. Sue's Paris thickens with plot here: Jesuit agents, lost heirs, and women caught between convent and world. Inside the serial's long game, the net around the Rennepont fortune draws tighter with every chapter.
3554-memoirs-of-napoleon-bonaparte-volum:
This fourth volume of Bourrienne's memoirs covers 1799 and 1800, from chapter twenty seven to chapter thirty five. The new government faces great difficulties, and Europe watches to see whether the First Consul can hold France together. Talleyrand becomes minister for foreign affairs, and Bonaparte opens talks with England and Austria that fail.

Bourrienne records Bonaparte's views on the East, his sacrifices to policy, and the denunciations that reached even the First Consul's own ear. The volume shows a ruler learning diplomacy after learning war. Readers get a close account of the Consulate's first months, when peace seemed possible and power was still being built.
3571-recollections-of-the-private-life-o:
Constant, Napoleon's first valet, turns in this fourth volume to the daily routine of the imperial household. He describes mornings in the palace, the dressing and shaving of the emperor, meals taken quickly between audiences, and the small staff who kept the household running. His view is that of a servant who saw Napoleon before the public mask went on.

The volume shows how much of empire was housekeeping: clothes, horses, letters, and timetables managed by trusted hands. Constant writes with loyalty and with pride in his own discretion. Readers who want Napoleon off the battlefield will find here the rhythms of court life, told by the man who stood closest to him each day.
3584-essays-of-michel-de-montaigne-volum:
This fourth volume of Montaigne's Essays holds chapters twenty two through twenty four of Book One. The first treats custom, arguing that we should not easily change a law once received, since habit gives laws their force. Montaigne illustrates the power of custom with a story of a countrywoman who grew used to carrying a young animal until it became a burden she could not set down.

The next chapters consider how the same counsel can lead to various events, and attack pedantry, the display of learning without judgment. Together they show Montaigne's conservatism about custom and his distrust of book learning divorced from life. The volume suits readers who want his most famous theme, the tyranny of habit, in short form.
3765-coniston-volume-04:
Winston Churchill brings Cynthia to Miss Sadler's school in the fourth book of Coniston, where girlhood friends in short dresses now seem far behind her. Life has already made a woman of her, and she carries a love she believes she must renounce, since Bob Worthington's father stands as an unjust man and a hypocrite. The thought is both sweet and bitter to her, sweet as judgment on the father, bitter because Bob is his son.

Cynthia weighs whether Bob's silence about his father's faults frees her to marry him, then tells herself the reasoning is false. The volume turns on conscience rather than action, with Boston parlors and school corridors as its stage. Readers who followed Cynthia from the tannery house will find her hardest trial here, fought in thought rather than in speech.
3904-the-confessions-of-jean-jacques-rou:
Jean Jacques Rousseau opens his fourth book with grief at not finding his friend on arrival, and regret at abandoning Le Maitre to misfortune. The musician's box, holding his whole fortune and the labor of his life, was seized at Lyons through Count Dortan. Even litigation was denied him, since superior strength decided the affair at once. Rousseau, young enough to find consolation quickly, still feels the loss.

The book then turns to his pastoral dream. His imagination ever leads him to Vaud by the lake, where an orchard, a firm friend, an amiable woman, a cow, and a little boat would make perfect happiness. He laughs at himself for seeking that dream among people of quite another disposition. Readers who like Rousseau's reveries will find wandering, loss, and longing in one book.
3917-serge-panine-volume-04:
Georges Ohnet's fourth volume of Serge Panine carries the novel toward its darker reckoning. The chapter titled Sin Grows Bolder opens at a party in Cayrol's mansion in the Rue Taitbout, where lights blaze and flowers crowd the drawing rooms. Cayrol, who has just lost his father, gives the party anyway and shows a smiling face, afraid that postponing it would rouse anxieties and harm his business.

Money dealings run beside the gaiety, as Herzog shakes hands with the Prince, promises results from his calculations on the money market, and goes to the cashier for scrip and a receipt. Matters have taken a turn for the worse during the last three days. Readers who follow Ohnet's society novel will find pleasure and ruin wearing the same evening dress.
5278-tales-and-novels-of-j-de-la-fontain:
Jean de La Fontaine's Tales and Novels continue in this fourth volume, in English verse translation. Its contents are The Old Man's Calendar, The Avaricious Wife and Tricking Galant, The Jealous Husband, and The Gascon Punished, each tale mocking the follies of marriage, money, and pride.

The Old Man's Calendar opens with surprise at how parents, arranging a daughter's marriage, mind riches above all else, leaving sweet sixteen to heaven's care. Readers get four sharp, bawdy tales in La Fontaine's ironic voice, where clever wives, jealous husbands, and boastful Gascons meet their comic deserts.
5359-the-inside-of-the-cup-volume-04:
Winston Churchill's Inside of the Cup continues in its fourth volume with chapters thirteen through sixteen: Winterbourne, A Saturday Afternoon, The Crucible, and Amid the Encircling Gloom. It opens with Hodder falling asleep from sheer exhaustion, waking at intervals to dreams in which the day's events return caricatured and distorted.

Alison Parr talks to the woman in the flat, and a familiar figure among romping, ragged children turns out to be Eldon Parr himself. This volume holds only this middle portion of the novel, in which Hodder's crisis deepens amid the gloom that encircles his parish.
5368-richard-carvel-volume-04:
Winston Churchill's Richard Carvel continues in its fourth volume with chapters nineteen through twenty-five. They are A Man of Destiny, A Sad Home-coming, The Gardener's Cottage, On the Road, London Town, Castle Yard, and The Rescue. It opens with Richard picked up and thrown into a brigantine's long-boat, head and stomach full of salt water, heart as light as spray.

This volume holds only this stretch of the novel, carrying Richard from the sea to London and a rescue. Readers following the story in order will find adventure, disguise. The road to the capital beckons, as Richard's fortunes turn on the sea and the city alike.
5377-a-modern-chronicle-volume-04:
Winston Churchill's Modern Chronicle continues in its fourth volume with a chapter of certain delicate matters. At Quicksands, the cult of Gad and Meni is practised with enthusiasm, and saints' days are polo days. The chief festival is the polo match against the Banbury Hunt Club, Quicksands's great rival, for more reasons than one, too delicate to tell.

The narrator recalls a Punch cartoon of Lord Beaconsfield performing an egg dance. He hopes to reach the chapter's end without breaking an egg. This volume holds only this Quicksands portion of Honora's story, in which sport, society, and delicate matters intertwine.
5386-the-celebrity-volume-04:
Winston Churchill's Celebrity continues in its fourth volume with chapter fifteen, in which the narrator decides that Mr Cooke shows at least some qualities of a great general. Hero-worship, he notes, has impelled rank and file in campaigns past and present, and so it was that morning, with their commander everywhere at once.

Cooke encourages his followers to work, holding over them the awful alternative of capture, and inoculating them with his own spirit. This volume holds only this late portion of Churchill's comedy. The pursuit of the Celebrity becomes a mock campaign, with generals, followers, and the threat of capture.
5391-the-crisis-volume-04:
Winston Churchill, the American novelist, carries The Crisis into the war years in this fourth volume. The narrator jumps ahead two years, describing a nation strained by conflict and a St. Louis community living under its pressure. Slavery, treated here as a disease planted in Virginia in 1620, becomes the moral center of the story.

Stephen Brice, a young lawyer, works in a busy office while the city around him changes under wartime strain. Newspaper work, legal clients, and daily life in a divided border city fill the chapters. Readers follow how ordinary people argued, endured, and chose sides as the war reshaped their world.
5412-the-memoirs-of-count-grammont-volum:
Anthony Hamilton's memoirs of Philibert de Grammont, edited with notes by Sir Walter Scott, reach the English court in this fourth volume. The chapters cover a comic adventure of the chaplain Poussetin, the story of the siege of Lerida, the marriage of the Duke of York, and other court details. Grammont tells the siege tale with relish, praising the Spanish defender Don Gregorio Brice as valiant as the Cid.

Court anecdote and military story sit side by side here, as they do throughout the memoirs. Readers hear how soldiers talked, how courtiers married, and how reputations traveled between France and England. It is a good entry point for anyone curious about Restoration courts without starting at the beginning.
5442-uarda-a-romance-of-ancient-egypt-vo:
Afternoon shadows grow long as a splendid chariot draws up to a terrace-temple in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Uarda. Paaker, the chief pioneer, drives handsome Syrian horses, with an Ethiopian slave behind him and his big dog running after the team. Called by name as he nears the temple, he checks his horses while a tiny man hurries up to him.

The arrival sets off the volume's temple intrigue, where rank, messages, and personal rivalries cross. Ebers fills the scene with chariots, animals, and ceremony. Readers follow the romance through a vivid Egyptian afternoon, where a grand entrance quickly turns into business.
5453-an-egyptian-princess-volume-04:
Three days before Nitetis is due to depart, Rhodopis invites many guests to her house at Naukratis in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's An Egyptian Princess. Croesus and Gyges are among them, while two lovers agree to meet in the garden under cover of darkness and an old slave, as the guests occupy themselves at the banquet. Melitta checks that the company is absorbed before the meeting.

The volume balances a glittering banquet with a secret garden tryst, as court politics and private feeling pull against each other. Ebers keeps both the feast and the lovers in view. Readers get a romantic, suspenseful stretch of the novel, where a farewell journey sharpens every stolen moment.
5476-cleopatra-volume-04:
Gorgias goes straight to his work in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Cleopatra, as twin statues wait to be raised before the Theatre of Dionysus. Dion seeks out his old friend, urged to talk with him before leaving the city with his betrothed bride. Since they parted, great building work has gone forward, including a wall on the Choma ordered by Antony.

The volume mixes friendship, art, and city building in ancient Alexandria, with lovers and builders planning their next steps. Ebers keeps sculpture, theater, and fortification in the foreground. Readers get a lively stretch of historical romance, where personal farewells meet public works.
5486-the-emperor-volume-04:
An emperor's body-slave starts up to help Selene, attacked by his sovereign's dog, in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's The Emperor. Something in that moment stays with him: an impression he cannot forget, with words and tones echoing in his mind and soul. He goes about his master's service afterward in a preoccupied, half-dreamy way.

The volume follows that inner disturbance through palace service, where a small incident unsettles a servant's whole world. Ebers gives the slave's feelings unusual weight beside imperial business. Readers get a psychological stretch of historical romance, showing Roman Alexandria from below as well as above.
5497-homo-sum-volume-04:
The light that attracted Paulus burns in Polykarp's room in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Homo Sum. That small upper story, built by the senator Petrus over the northern part of his house's flat roof, belongs to his son. Polykarp arrived about noon with slaves he had just procured, learned all that happened in his absence, and fell silent.

The volume follows a son's return to a household full of news, where silence says more than speech. Ebers keeps the desert town's families and their servants close at hand. Readers get a quiet, tense stretch of the early Christian romance, centered on homecoming and withheld feeling.
5504-serapis-volume-04:
Dada spends a swift, happy day under the roof of Medius in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Serapis, looking over costumes and scenery in wonderful variety. The children are bright and friendly, and they delight in her little tricks and rhymes, which Papias already knows by heart. She also enjoys watching the domestic troubles of the singer's household.

The volume follows performers and their families in late Roman Egypt, where theater, children, and household worries mix. Ebers gives the backstage world warmth and detail. Readers get a charming stretch of historical romance, centered on a young performer finding a place among new friends.
5511-arachne-volume-04:
Outside a tent door, Hermon tries to banish Althea's image from his mind in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Arachne. He feels foolish for overrating the miserable actress last night, a woman who has lost all charm for him, even as a model for his Arachne. He would rather face his pure friend with stains on his robe than mastered by yearning for the Thracian woman.

The first glance at Daphne's beloved face and the first words of her greeting teach him otherwise, restoring a cleaner feeling. The volume turns on an artist's remorse and renewal. Readers get a reflective stretch of the romance, where a sculptor judges his own desire and chooses again.
5520-the-bride-of-the-nile-volume-04:
Paula's report of the day's events, Orion's behavior, and the trial's results angers the leech beyond measure in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's The Bride of the Nile. He strongly approves the girl's resolve to quit this cave of robbers, this house of wickedness, treachery, imbecile judges, and false witnesses, as soon as possible. But she finds no chance for a quiet talk with him, since Philippus soon has his hands full.

The volume turns on a corrupt trial and a young woman's decision to leave a dangerous household. Ebers writes Byzantine Egypt as a place of courts, kin, and intrigue. Readers get an indignant, suspenseful stretch of the romance, where justice fails and flight looks like sense.
5533-a-thorny-path-volume-04:
Melissa would probably have become a prisoner herself in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's A Thorny Path. Instead Zminis, balked of a triumph and beside himself with rage, rushed after the fugitive with the rest. She has no further need to seek the house where her lover lies, since Agatha knows it well. Its owner, Proterius, belongs illustriously to the Christian community, and Agatha often visited him with her father.

The volume follows pursuit, refuge, and Christian households in Caracalla's Alexandria, where a girl's safety depends on friends who know the right doors. Ebers keeps the chase tense. Readers get a suspenseful stretch of the romance, where a fugitive's friends make the difference.
5555-margery-gred-a-tale-of-old-nurember:
Margery and her party reach the forest lodge that evening with red faces and half-frozen hands and feet in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Margery, a tale of old Nuremberg. The ride through deep snow and bitter December wind was hard, but woods in glittering winter dress, sharp pure air, and trifling matters reward them. White hats crown every stock and stone, and tiny snow crystals fall on green velvet.

The volume follows a winter journey to a forest lodge, with cold, beauty, and small wonders in balance. Ebers writes winter travel in Margery's voice. Readers get a crisp, atmospheric stretch of the tale, where hardship and loveliness arrive together.
5564-barbara-blomberg-volume-04:
Old Ursel had exclaimed, Poor Wolf. Yet whoever met the young knight next morning climbing to the Blombergs' rooms would have thought him the happiest of mortals. He seemed the equal of Baron Malfalconnet in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's Barbara Blomberg. He obeyed Dr. Hiltner's summons and stayed long with him, then hurried home at a rapid pace, longing to tell Barbara how fair a prospect for their future had opened.

The volume follows a knight's sudden happiness after a doctor's news, with love and future prospects brightening. Ebers writes the change of mood from pity to joy. Readers get a hopeful stretch of the romance, where a morning visit transforms a young man's outlook.
5575-a-word-only-a-word-volume-04:
The admiral's ship bearing King Philip's ambassador to Venice reaches its destination safely in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's A Word, Only a Word, despite severe storms on the voyage. Ulrich, the only passenger who stays as well as an old sailor amid rolling and pitching, suffers in peace of mind instead. Watchers seeing him lean over the bulwark, gaze into the sea, or pace with restless bearing and gloomy eyes would scarcely suspect the youth within.

The volume follows a reserved, irritable young man across a stormy sea toward Venice, with inner turmoil matching the weather. Ebers writes travel as character study. Readers get a brooding stretch of the romance, where a safe landing brings no peace.
5581-the-burgomaster-s-wife-volume-04:
The burgomaster's wife worries about Henrica in the fourth volume of Georg Ebers's The Burgomaster's Wife. Henrica greets her with special cheerfulness and meets gentle reproaches by saying the morning did her good. Fate is just, she says, and if confidence of recovery helps the physician, Doctor Bontius will have an easy task with her. A dead Castilian must be the wretch who plunged her into her present state.

The volume follows a young woman's brave front during the siege, with a doctor, a dead enemy, and a household's worry in play. Ebers writes illness and courage together. Readers get a moving stretch of the siege romance, where cheerfulness itself is an act of resistance.
5596-the-story-of-my-life-volume-04:
Georg Ebers recalls the founders of the Keilhau Institute in the fourth volume of his autobiography, The Story of My Life, from childhood to manhood. He knew all three founders well: Friedrich Froebel, Middendorf, and Langethal, with the latter two as his teachers. Froebel, already sixty-six when Ebers came to Keilhau, was decidedly the master who planned it, a man of lofty purpose.

The volume glimpses the school's history through its founders, showing how a famous educational experiment shaped a boy. Ebers writes memory with gratitude. Readers get a vivid stretch of autobiography, where a great educator appears as a living teacher, not a legend.
5648-sketches-by-seymour-volume-04:
Seymour's Sketches, part four, opens with Watty Williams and the bull. Watty, a studious youth with a long nose and short trousers, delights in green fields, finding sermons in stones and good in everything. Wandering a meadow lost in Zimmerman on Solitude, he hears a loud moo and turns to see a curly-fronted bull making toward him, to his dismay.

Watty, good-humored enough to laugh at an Irish bull and staunch in his views, must now face a real one. The sketches that follow keep that comic collision of philosophy and farm life. Readers get Victorian illustrated humor, gentle, absurd, and full of country mishaps.
5667-the-arabian-nights-entertainments-v:
Volume four of the Aldine Arabian Nights, from Jonathan Scott's text and printed in London in 1890, closes the set with some of its best-known wonders. Its contents include the enchanted horse. Prince Ahmed and the fairy Perie Banou appear, as do sisters who envied their younger sister. Three sharpers, a sultan, princes, viziers, and travellers fill further tales. As in earlier volumes, stories nest inside stories, each one buying time and wonder.

Readers will find flying devices, hidden treasure, jealousy, and clever escapes, all told with the brisk pace of tales meant to be heard aloud. The volume rewards dipping in anywhere, since most tales stand alone. It also rewards reading straight through. Themes of fate, gratitude, and trickery echo from one story to the next. It is a fitting close to a collection built on the power of a tale well told.
5691-the-innocents-abroad-volume-04:
Part four of Mark Twain's Innocents Abroad covers chapters thirty-one through forty, and it opens in the buried city of Pompeii. Twain confesses he had pictured torchlit tunnels and gloomy passages, like a silver mine, and then corrects that fancy against the open streets and ruined houses he actually walks. The gap between imagined Pompeii and real Pompeii sets the comic tone.

We travel with the pilgrims through Italian ruins, relics, and local guides, hearing Twain puncture both guidebook romance and tourist awe. The part balances real observation with jokes about what visitors expect to feel. It stands as vivid travel writing on its own, and it deepens the book's long joke about Americans abroad meeting history face to face.
577-the-works-of-samuel-johnson-in-sixte:
Samuel Johnson's fourth volume in this sixteen-volume set pairs two of his great periodical works, The Rambler and The Adventurer. Johnson wrote the Rambler essays largely alone, twice a week, on morals, books, and life. Johnson wrote the Rambler from 1750 to 1752, largely alone and under deadline.

The Adventurer, written with friends, adds lighter pieces to the same serious purpose. Together the essays show Johnson the moralist at his fullest, in prose that is weighty, balanced, and often unexpectedly witty. The Adventurer, shared with friends, lightened the load without losing Johnson's moral seriousness.
5785-a-tramp-abroad-volume-04:
Volume four of Mark Twain's A Tramp Abroad covers chapters twenty-two through twenty-eight, from the Black Forest to the Rigi-Kulm. Chapters introduce a grandee and his family. A wealthy nabob, a new standard of wealth, and a skeleton for a new novel follow. The book then turns to natural history and the ant as a fraud. A day's tramp, Sunday on the continent, Lucerne and its lake, and the glacier garden follow.

A journey with Twain through German and Swiss scenery, hearing him mock guidebooks, grand tourists, and his own party in equal measure. The Rigi ascent caps the volume with mountain comedy and real grandeur side by side. It suits readers who enjoy Twain's walking chapters, where a day's tramp produces a day's worth of jokes and observations.
5906-the-history-of-don-quixote-volume-1:
A terrific battle concludes and finishes in chapter nine of this Don Quixote portion, between the gallant Biscayan and the valiant Manchegan. The history had left them with drawn swords uplifted, ready to deliver furious slashing blows, and chapter nine resolves that suspended combat. Chapter ten offers pleasant discourse between Quixote and Sancho, chapter eleven what befell him with goatherds, and chapter twelve a goatherd's relation.

Chapter thirteen ends the story of the shepherdess Marcela, with other incidents, closing the pastoral episode. Readers get Cervantes's mix of swordplay, talk, and shepherds' tales, as the knight's road alternates between blows and stories. This part suits readers following Quixote in order, since Marcela's tale tests chivalric ideals against a woman's freedom to refuse.
6198-cumner-s-son-and-other-south-sea-fo:
A Sable Spartan opens Parker's fourth South Sea volume, as Lady Tynemouth shows interest and his Excellency amusement, real interest and un-ironical amusement, at Blithelygo's luncheon talk. He claims uniform revolutionizes the savage: put him in convention, that is clothes, give him responsibility, that is vanity and power, and you make a Britisher.

Blithelygo, clever in his way, knows military matters, good cigars, and pretty women, yet would give up both sooner than a fixed idea. Deferential yet willing to argue a minor point, he holds the table. Only the fourth South Sea set is discussed in this entry, with the remaining South Sea sets left undescribed here.
6246-the-right-of-way-volume-04:
A fierce storm breaks over the Chaudiere valley, tearing fences, carrying off small bridges, and whitening the ground with hail. It marches through the forest to Vadrome Mountain, felling trees and drowning the cries of birds, then passes into the next parish and leaves a shining calm behind. In the house on the mountain, the tailor of Chaudiere watches with sympathy, for the storm matches his own feelings after months of hard fighting.

This fourth volume drives Charley toward a wild ride, a warning from Rosalie, and a stand at bay, with Jo Portugais telling a story and a challenge from Paulette Dubois. The Cure and the Seigneur visit the tailor, and the chapters close as things stood at the start. Parker lets weather and will mirror each other, storm outside and storm within.
6773-the-thirty-years-war-volume-04:
Book four of Schiller's Thirty Years' War begins after Gustavus Adolphus dies, dissolving the weak bond that held Protestant members of the empire together. Allies stand free again, and must form their union anew, or lose all gains bought with blood and fall one by one to an enemy they could master only together. Neither Sweden nor any single German state can match emperor and league alone.

Peace sought now, Schiller warns, would mean taking laws from the foe. The book that follows traces the allies' hard choice between new union and ruin. Book four is the turning point of Schiller's history, where victory's fruits hang in doubt.
6779-history-of-the-revolt-of-the-nether:
Book four of Schiller's Revolt of the Netherlands, on the iconoclasts, opens by questioning how far back the outbreak's springs should be traced. French Protestants, Schiller allows, likely worked to raise a nursery for their faith in the Netherlands and to keep Spain busy at home, urging their oppressed brethren on with daring hopes. Agents in the provinces fanned anger against the ruling church.

By stressing oppression, they hurried folk imperceptibly into illegal courses, Schiller argues, with care for motive and fact. The book that follows traces the image-breaking storm itself. Book four is a measured account of religious fury and its political roots.
6953-by-england-s-aid-or-the-freeing-of-:
G A Henty tells the second phase of Holland's war of independence, when England openly joined the struggle. His preface recalls a promise made in By Pike and Dyke, which had carried the story to the death of the Prince of Orange and the capture of Antwerp. That first volume kept the scene among the low lands and cities of Holland and Zeeland, where a defensive war faced overpowering odds.

Now England, long an unofficial helper, throws herself into the strife, and the war grows far wider in scope. Henty writes for lads, with battles, sieges, and brave captains at the fore. The tale follows the freeing of the Netherlands from 1585 to 1604, when English aid helped turn a stubborn defense into success.
7589-the-caxtons-a-family-picture-volume:
Part four of The Caxtons centers on a household morning and a sudden leave-taking. The narrator praises rising early, treating the first hours as the freshest part of the day, while late, idle mornings look like youth already worn out. A walk then carries him past his father's study and into family business. The mood is reflective before it turns practical.

The practical turn comes from an uncle, offended or merely restless, who orders his chaise and pair and announces that he leaves today. Around that exit, Lytton balances moral talk about habit with small domestic drama. The part shows the Caxton house at its most characteristic: thought at breakfast, feeling soon after, and a family adjusting to one member's abrupt decision.
7612-eugene-aram-volume-04:
Book four of Eugene Aram runs Walter's adventure beside Aram's darker story, and Lytton keeps both threads taut. Walter's tale is pure adventure: a robbery and escape on the road. The chapter heads promise Walter's thanks to Fillgrave, the corporal's counsel and triumph, and a motto from Gil Blas on physicians and their censurers.

The attack itself is sudden and brutal. Walter, left in a situation so critical that delay would be inhuman, is felled by a blow that stuns him for an instant. His strong frame, and the peril itself, recall him from momentary insensibility. A ruffian, leaning down, lays a hand on his heart and cries that he is dead, while the traveler, flesh creeping at the touch, prudently abstains from motion or exclamation. Survival here is a matter of stillness.
7618-pelham-volume-04:
Pelham returns to London in this part, changed by a year away. He takes rooms at Mivart's and finds his mind altered: pleasure no longer satisfies him for its own sake. He now covets its enjoyments as sources of worldly distinction.

The narrator admits he is no less a coxcomb than before, and no less a voluptuary in taste. But ambition has joined vanity in him. Clothes, tailors, and society matter, and the part tracks a young man learning to turn polish into power. London society, with its dinners and drawing rooms, becomes his new school.
7627-devereux-volume-04:
Book four of Devereux turns on recovery and accusation, as the hero regains his mind just as danger closes round him. Justice has searched in vain for the murderers, and the packet is gone. Suspicion rests on Gerald, whom the loss benefits, but Gerald comes forward boldly to meet inquiry. A clear mind returns just when the danger grows sharpest, and the part uses that timing well.

The recovery itself opens the book, framed as a re-entrance into life through affliction. Months pass before the hero's senses return. He rises from a bed of suffering and madness calm, collected, and immovable, altered but tranquil. That calm, set against an open accusation, is the part's tension: a man newly steady, facing a charge he must meet with his wits intact.
7634-the-disowned-volume-04:
Talbot counsels Clarence seriously in this part of The Disowned. Lady Westborough has forbidden him the boudoir, but Talbot insists a boudoir is a very different thing from a daughter. The veto, he argues, need not extend to both.

More deeply, Talbot urges Clarence to end his incognito and resume his proper name. He has tasted the pleasures and the pains of living under a borrowed identity. The part turns on a choice: keep hiding, or claim the name and fortune that are rightfully his. A name, once resumed, cannot easily be laid down again.
7643-ernest-maltravers-volume-04:
Alice Darvil's hard road fills Book Four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Ernest Maltravers. While the hero pursues learning in comfort, Alice walks a rough path as a poor child with no guide but need. Poetry and science offer her no shelter on the common highway of life.

Later chapters show her as Mrs. Butler, winning respect in a town far from her past, yet warned that her own name could cost her child and home. The volume pairs her plain struggle with Maltravers' fine thoughts, and asks what a woman with no money or rank must give up to stay safe.
7653-kenelm-chillingly-volume-04:
More than a year after Kenelm left England, Book Four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Kenelm Chillingly returns to London in the sociable weeks before Easter. At Lord Beaumanoir's conversazione, small parties still allow real talk among writers, artists, and men of rank, before the crowded season dries talk up.

Kenelm's kin debate his strange course, and the volume weighs the old Chillingly spirit against cold modern times. Wit, family pride, and the clash of ideal hopes with party politics fill these chapters, as the hero's absence shapes every room he has left.
7662-what-will-he-do-with-it-volume-04:
Gloom settles over Gatesboro' in Book Four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's What Will He Do With It? Mayor Hartopp locks his ledgers with a sullen face, and the mood spreads through warehouse, tan yard, shops, and his own villa. Some shock has struck the whole town at once.

Amid the unease, a strong-wristed stranger saves a lady from harm and talks with Mrs. Haughton about her son's wish for the army and the generous Mr. Darrell. The volume blends town comedy, social rank, and hidden ties, as small-town order cracks under a secret no one will name.
7688-lucretia-volume-04:
Part Two of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Lucretia opens after the storm of revolution has passed: Napoleon's puppet dynasties have crumbled, the plough crosses Waterloo, and harvests shine over an empire's grave. Only one small track through that vast change holds the reader's eye.

On a terrace at Laughton a lone step paces, for the bride no longer clings to her groom's arm. Charles Vernon sleeps in the St. John vault, having lived longer than doctors hoped, cheerful to the end. The volume turns from public upheaval to private loss and the long shadow of youth.
7695-a-strange-story-volume-04:
Dr. Fenwick hurries to a fevered child in the fourth volume of Edward Bulwer Lytton's A Strange Story, a boy hurt by Margrave's carelessness and now delirious. The doctor forgets his own haunting thoughts in a night of prompt, simple remedies, staying to comfort the parents till danger passes.

At gray dawn he walks home through clear air, and the tale turns to Haroun, a healer of unknown birth whose cures aim to rally life itself against disease. A letter to Lilian also appears, flighty yet earnest. Medicine, mystery, and guilt intertwine in these chapters.
7705-my-novel-volume-04:
Marriage fills the opening debate of Book Four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's My Novel, as Mr. Caxton praises Pisistratus for showing Riccabocca's love in one stroke: he leaves off his spectacles. An uncle counters with Shakespeare's slovenly lover, and the family weighs which sign fits which kind of passion.

Blanche calls Miss Jemima forward, and Mrs. Caxton worries for the dignity of her sex. Later a parson seeks the Avenels, facing a stiff maid and a mild old man in a small parlor. The volume blends learned talk with country manners and a courtship watched by all.
7718-the-last-of-the-barons-volume-04:
Robert Hilyard, still in priest's disguise, threads dingy Thames alleys in Book Four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's The Last of the Barons, subtitled Intrigues of the Court of Edward IV. Disbanded men of either Rose lounge by plaster huts, ready for any job where steel wins gold.

He knocks at a poor house of a religious order, where a foreign priest lodges, and the plot thickens. Later, Prince and Montagu spar over a joust meant to slight Warwick, while the young prince bears a champion's helm despite his grudge at the Woodvilles. Court games mask real enmity.
7731-paul-clifford-volume-04:
Clifford, Tomlinson, and Pepper skip a fine Milsom Street lodging in the fourth volume of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Paul Clifford, heading instead for a mean alehouse in a remote suburb. An elderly dame opens the door, and Ned calls for drink and pipes with rough good humor.

Old Mr. Bags has just gone out for more work, and the three worthies settle to wait for their fellows. Through slang, jest, and a newspaper read aloud, the volume shows the robbers' fellowship at ease, a world of loyalty and low cunning far from Bath's gay rooms.
7740-the-parisians-volume-04:
Isaura Cicogna writes to Madame de Grantmesnil in Book Four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's The Parisians, after days of silence under the spell of Savarin's words. An author parting from a finished work, he says, bids farewell to a companion who can never again talk familiarly once the world owns it.

Isaura feels the truth of that awe, as a book that held all her hopes dies to its maker at birth. Later she and an Englishman find they have chosen the same favorite star, a small coincidence that delights Savarin's circle. Art, fame, and tender feeling intertwine here.
7904-american-historical-and-literary-cu: For part four of American Historical and Literary Curiosities by John Jay Smith and John F. Watson, the text file offers only the editor's note and the title page. Since the series consists of illustrations and page images, with few sections that scan well as text, the note sends readers to the HTML file where the plates can be seen.
8679-by-england-s-aid-or-the-freeing-of-:
G. A. Henty continues his Dutch war story in By England's Aid, covering the freeing of the Netherlands from 1585 to 1604. His preface recalls that By Pike and Dyke promised a sequel: the first book carried the struggle to the death of the Prince of Orange and the capture of Antwerp. This volume takes up the second phase, when England, long an unofficial helper of Holland, steps in more openly. An illustration shows Geoffrey and Lionel saving Francis Vere's life.

Young English volunteers fight beside Dutch troops against Spain, through sieges, marches, and sea actions. Henty blends real commanders and battles with invented heroes, teaching history through adventure in his usual brisk style. Readers get a readable outline of the later Dutch revolt, and a boys' book that treats alliance, courage, and Protestant cause as the stuff of heroism.
8782-the-divine-comedy-by-dante-illustra:
This fourth part of Cary's Inferno covers cantos seven and eight, the circles of the avaricious and the wrathful. Canto seven opens with Plutus crying, ah me, O Satan, Satan, in hoarse alarm, while Virgil, whom no event surprises, comforts Dante and commands the cursed wolf to turn its fury inward. Hoarders and spendthrifts roll great weights against each other, and the sullen lie in a marsh of mud.

Canto eight crosses the Styx toward the city of Dis, where devils refuse the travellers entry and Dante's anger flares against a Florentine enemy sunk in the mire. The part shows Hell growing darker and more political, as personal hatred joins theological punishment. Virgil's calm authority steadies the pilgrim, and the reader, through threats that will soon need Heaven's help to pass. It is a tense, dramatic stretch of the descent.
911-commission-report-2004:
Congress and President George W. Bush created the 9/11 Commission to explain the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001. The bipartisan panel, led by Thomas Kean and Lee Hamilton, held public hearings and reviewed millions of pages of records. Its final report appeared in July 2004 and became a bestseller, unusual for a government document.

The narrative traces the plot from its roots in Afghanistan to the morning of the attacks, and shows how agencies failed to share what they knew. The report blamed a failure of imagination across the government. Its proposals drove a major overhaul of American intelligence, including a new director over all the spy agencies. It stands as the main official history of the attacks.
9308-new-york-at-the-louisiana-purchase-:
Delancey Ellis compiled this official report in 1907 on New York at the Louisiana Purchase Exposition in St. Louis in 1904. The report, sent to Governor Charles Hughes in March 1907, bears the names of the state commission, from Edward Harriman to Charles Ball, secretary and chief executive officer. Chapters give history, exhibits, and finance.

New York's display at the great fair showed the state's commerce, arts, and progress to the nation. Ellis sets out the work in order, with cross-references updated from page numbers to chapters. The volume remains a useful record of world's fair history, and of New York's pride in 1904.
9439-tales-and-novels-volume-04:
Maria Edgeworth's fourth volume of Tales and Novels, printed in 1857, mixes a famous Irish novel with sharp essays. Castle Rackrent, told by the steward Thady Quirk, follows a line of rackety landlords through debt and folly. Beside it stand an essay on Irish bulls, a jesting essay on self-justification, and the tales Ennui and The Dun. Edgeworth's wit and Irish ear run through all five pieces.

Thady's voice, loyal yet sly, lets the reader see the Rackrents ruin themselves while praising them. The essays poke fun at Irish speech traps and at the art of excuse-making. Ennui and The Dun add tales of bored wealth and debt's grip. A reader gets a landmark of Irish fiction plus satire, in one handy volume of a master storyteller.
9766-alice-or-the-mysteries-book-04:
Book four of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Alice, or The Mysteries, opens days after Lord Vargrave's interview with Maltravers. Mr. Cleveland arrives at Burleigh, a cheerful, urbane old gentleman, gout permitting. Cleveland's sensible talk pleases, yet his worldly philosophy chills an imaginative hearer. The book weighs reason against feeling, as its lovers' fates tangle.

Cleveland's arrival relieves Burleigh's solitude, but his rational views bound the scope of hope. Lytton writes with polished care for manners and motive. A reader gets the fourth book of a Victorian mystery romance, where a sensible friend tests a hero's deeper faith.
a-modern-chronicle-volume-04:
Winston Churchill's A Modern Chronicle, volume four, continues Book Two at chapter seven, Of Certain Delicate Matters. Quicksands worships Gad and Meni, Churchill's biblical names for luck and money, and its saints' days are polo days. The Banbury Hunt Club match is the festival of festivals. Honora, an heretic in this cult, watches the libations poured.

Of Mental Processes — Feminine and Insoluble turns inward, and a revolutionizing vehicle arrives with the motor age. On the Art of Lion Taming treats the management of great men as social sport. Containing Some Revelations closes the volume's five chapters. Churchill's satire of Long Island wealth is at its broadest here: temples like yellow fungi, shekels laid aside, and a heroine quietly losing faith. Book Two is the chronicle of a marriage inside the money cult, and the revelations prepare its breaking.
a-select-bibliography-of-chemistry-1492-:
A Select Bibliography of Chemistry, 1492-1902, published in 1904, is the later extension of Henry Carrington Bolton's bibliography of chemical literature. Issued as a Smithsonian publication, it contains the titles of books published between 1898 and 1902, carrying Bolton's four-century survey forward to the new century. Most of the proofreading, and the preparation of the index, was done by Axel Moth.

Bolton had mapped chemistry's printed record from 1492 onward in his earlier volumes, and this supplement keeps the map current. It lists the newest chemical books of its five-year span in the same order as the main work. For historians it completes the Bolton set, the standard guide to chemical literature before the age of abstract journals.
a-thorny-path-volume-04:
Georg Ebers sets two girls walking together in Volume 4 of A Thorny Path, and a case of mistaken identity becomes a friendship. Ebers explains that Melissa nearly fell into prison herself, but the hunter Zminis rushed after a fugitive and left her free. Agatha, a Christian girl, knows the house where Melissa's lover lies, and guides her through streets neither should walk at such an hour.

Chapter XI lets the girls trade stories on the way. Agatha is often taken for her dead cousin, the lost daughter of Seleukus, whose family split when part of it embraced Christianity. Both girls have lost their mothers, and the shared grief pulls them close fast. They clasp hands and walk on like sisters. In a divided city, that instant trust is its own quiet argument.
a-tramp-abroad-volume-04:
The Black Forest grandee waits in A Tramp Abroad, Part 4, by Mark Twain. Twain gives Chapter XXII to the wealthy peasant household, its family, and its riches, drawn with the same care he gives to princes elsewhere. A day's tramp and talk follow, then a chapter on Sunday on the continent, where the day of rest is kept in ways that puzzle an American raised on silent Sabbaths.

Lucerne and its lake open the Swiss half, with a wild chamois, the commerce of the town, and a bit of history about martyrdom's benefits. The Glacier Garden and an excursion on the lake lead to the Rigi-Kulm, whose ascent Twain describes under the heading Stripping for Business. The joke is structural: every sublime view in this book is reached by the least sublime arrangements, and Twain reports both halves honestly.
a-word-only-a-word-volume-04:
Georg Ebers sends Ulrich to sea in Volume 4 of A Word, Only a Word, aboard an admiral's ship bound for Venice. Ebers writes that the vessel carried King Philip's ambassador and weathered many hard storms on the way. Ulrich, alone among the passengers, stayed as well as an old sailor through the rolling and pitching, yet his peace of mind took the real damage in this volume.

Chapter XXI looks back at the hopes he boarded with. Isabella's life was to join his, and Italy was to be a paradise of art wandered freely, studio to studio, until he chose a new master. Sophonisba's home was meant to receive him. Now orders, duties, and a fixed course hem the journey in. The sea crossing becomes a measure of how far a young artist's boldest dreams can bend before they break.
adams-mont-saint-michel-1904:
In 1904 Henry Adams published a study of two great churches of medieval France, Mont Saint Michel and Chartres. He wrote it first for his nieces, in a warm and personal voice. Adams had already toured both sites and knew their stones and stories well. The book treats stone, glass, and prayer as one work of art.

Adams reads the abbey and the cathedral as signs of a world held together by faith in the Virgin Mary. He sets that unity against the split and driven world he knew in his own time. Lovers of Gothic building still turn to it as a classic guide.
an-egyptian-princess-volume-04:
An Egyptian Princess reaches Volume 4 with Georg Ebers still braiding romance and royal politics in the ancient East. Ebers drew on his Egyptology, meaning his study of ancient Egypt, to dress the tale. Nitetis is about to leave Egypt for Persia, and the farewell days at Naukratis carry the action here.

Chapter XI brings guests to the house of Rhodopis, among them Croesus and Gyges. In the garden, Sappho meets her lover in secret, helped by an old slave who watches for intruders. The lovers count their last three days together and dread the parting. Their quiet scene plays against banquets and state plans, so love and empire press on the same small group of friends.
andreyev-red-laugh-1904:
The Red Laugh reached English in Alexandra Linden's translation, first issued in 1905 from Leonid Andreyev's Russian of 1904. The book calls itself fragments of a discovered manuscript. An officer in the Russo-Japanese War records heat, thirst, shellfire, and madness in broken notes that slide toward vision.

The red laugh itself is his name for the grinning horror of the war as a whole. A second part follows his brother home, where peace proves as haunted as the front. Andreyev wrote before war literature had a modern form, and he found one in fever and fragment. The book became an early landmark of anti-war writing in Europe. Its method shaped later expressionist prose.
arabian-nights-burton-1885-vol-04:
Volume four of Burton's Thousand Nights and a Night came out in 1885 with the rest of the main set. Shahrazad's sister Dinarzad keeps asking for one more tale before dawn. The king keeps listening, and the pile of stories within stories grows deeper with every night.

Burton renders the Arabic with deliberate closeness, keeping proverbs, verses, and oaths intact. His notes on law, custom, and daily life in the East fill the margins of the text. The middle volumes of the set reward steady readers most: patterns of fate and cleverness repeat with fresh faces. Burton printed the work for subscribers, since its frankness barred the open market.
arabian-nights-burton-supplemental-1886-:
Burton's fourth supplemental volume, issued in the late 1880s, continues his gathering of Nights tales from side manuscripts. By this point the project had become the largest English rendering of Arabic story ever attempted. The tales here extend Shahrazad's world with fresh kings, quests, and enchantments in her familiar manner.

Burton's notes remain a second book running under the first, full of parallels from his travels. He served in India, Arabia, and Africa, and his comparisons draw on all three. The Gutenberg text of this volume is ebook 3448. Few Victorian translations match this one's stamina. Volume four keeps the supplement's standard: nothing cut, nothing softened, everything annotated.
arachne-volume-04:
Arachne reaches a tender turn in Volume 4, where Georg Ebers brings the sculptor Hermon back to Daphne. Ebers sets the scene outside her tent, with Hermon trying to shake off Althea, a Thracian actress who had served as his model. Her image, he decides, has lost its hold, and he dreads meeting his friend while still tangled in that longing.

Chapter XIV gives Daphne the first word, and it is a gentle reproach. She tells him plainly that he neglected her almost past courtesy, yet offers pardon with no trace of bitterness. Her companion Chrysilla, busy knotting fringe into cloth she wove herself, keeps a careful watch over the pair. Forgiveness here is quick, but it is not careless, and the artist must still earn back lost trust.
arxiv-2509-00404:
Hengjie Cao leads a team of sixteen authors who present Metis in 2025, a framework for training large language models with four-bit floating point quantization. Quantization rounds numbers to a coarse grid to save compute. The barrier to low-bit training is anisotropy in singular value spectra, where a few huge values stretch the numeric range and distort the signal.

Metis works in the spectral domain, splitting such spectra into narrower sub-distributions that are quantized separately. Two traits of the dominant spectral subspace, its preservation under sparse random sampling and under random projection, keep decomposition cost negligible. On an eight-billion-parameter LLaMA-3 model trained on one hundred billion tokens, the method holds up at four-bit precision.
arxiv-2509-01004:
Soham Ghosh, with two co-authors, proposes a quantum physical unclonable function, or QPUF, based on chaotic Hamiltonians. QPUFs are hardware-based cryptographic tools. Their security stems from modeling them as Haar-random unitaries. Building such unitaries on current quantum devices is hard. Simulation cost grows exponentially with system size.

The new design models the QPUF as time evolution under a chaotic Hamiltonian. The team proves security comparable to the Haar-random case. Chaotic dynamics generate less randomness than the ideal. Yet it suffices to make the device unclonable in polynomial time. Evolution time scales linearly with the number of qudits. It can also be kept public safely. The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model is named as a candidate.
arxiv-2509-01604:
Disease and environmental data are often gathered by area, again and again over long spans, and local trends matter for decisions. Alejandro Rozo Posada, with six co-authors, proposes a Bayesian model for such areal time series. Each area gets its own Gaussian process for its time path, a flexible curve model, while spatial links enter through the processes' settings, which are themselves correlated across space.

Neighbors thus share information about how their temporal patterns behave, while keeping distinct local trajectories. That structure offers an alternative way to represent how space and time interact. Inference runs through Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. Rozo Posada and the team aim for sharper local trend estimates with honest uncertainty, supporting surveillance and public health choices that depend on knowing when one place truly diverges from its neighbors.
arxiv-2509-01804:
Yifan Lan, Xin Cai, Jun Cheng, and Shan Tan tackle image sorting when some classes are rare and others are common. Such long-tailed data, where a few classes dominate, trips up deep networks trained on it. Their tool is the information bottleneck, a method that squeezes inputs while keeping label relevant detail. They add loss rebalancing and self teaching steps to protect rare classes.

A mixture version runs several bottlenecks that draw on different network layers at once. Training then learns features and sorting together from an information theory view. Tests on three standard long-tailed sets, including a large nature photo set, reach top scores. Both the single and mixture versions beat prior methods in their checks.
arxiv-2509-01904:
Chunguo Duan leads ten co-authors in the first systematic hunt for acetamide in massive star forming cores. Acetamide is an amide molecule tied to formamide, and amides matter for prebiotic chemistry, the steps toward life. Past finds were sparse, leaving its spread unclear. The survey uses a large radio array across fifty-two hot cores where complex molecules thrive.

Acetamide appears in ten cores, greatly expanding the known source list. Amounts span a wide range, and ratios to formamide stay near constant across sources. That steady link hints both form on grain surfaces through a shared route. Finding peptide like molecules surviving star birth supports a path from space chemistry to early life ingredients.
arxiv-2509-02204:
Dario Ruggiero, Mauro Mancini, and Elisa Capello give a smart steer plan for low thrust craft in a ring shaped shared orbit. Near tasks like fleet flight and checks of lone craft need sharp state reads. Their watcher tweaks its own gains based on the state it reads at the time. That tweak aims at fast settle with low noise pull at the same time.

A Lyapunov based proof backs the calm and truth of the state reads. Sims with sight based sensor data test the plan in near real terms. Next to old watchers with fixed gains, path track truth jumps up by a lot. Switch of thrust drops too, which cuts wear on the drive in flight. The plan suits self led place and steer work near lone targets.
arxiv-2509-02704:
Marius Bargo and Yacouba Simpore wrote a 2025 paper on age-structured food webs. Their nonlinear model tracks several species by age. Interactions inside and between species are shaped by environmental factors. Harvesting is the control lever.

Under general assumptions, the authors prove solutions exist. The solutions are unique and stay positive. The assumptions cover interaction kernels, mortality, and reproduction rates. A cyclic competition example shows a striking result. Species chase each other in a rock-paper-scissors loop there. Control applied to one species can stabilise the whole system globally. A second case targets malaria mosquitoes. It uses biological and genetic control strategies. For the biological route, an explicit Lyapunov function proves global stability of the aquatic stage.
arxiv-2509-02804:
Feng-Yi Liao and Yang Zheng proposed a 2025 optimization method for a broad class of rough problems. Optimization means searching for the lowest value of some cost. Their target functions are weakly convex, a loose form of bowl-shaped that still covers many hard, non-smooth cases.

Their method mixes two older ideas: stepping through nearby proxy problems and keeping a bundle of simple local models. The analysis gives clear bounds on how much work is needed to reach a near-stationary point, where progress stalls. One notable trait is automatic adaptivity, meaning the method speeds up on its own when a problem turns out smoother. Under stronger growth conditions it can even settle at a steady linear pace.
arxiv-2509-03104:
Leonid Kondrashov and 3 co-authors measured hidden overheads in serverless cloud computing in a 2025 systems study. Serverless platforms run short pieces of code on demand, so providers must keep spare capacity warm and ready. Autoscaling policies decide how much spare capacity to hold, trading speed against cost.

The team built an open system that mimics two major commercial platforms, then replayed real workloads while varying the scaling settings. Instance churn, the constant starting and stopping of workers, burned a large share of computing cycles. Memory held in reserve ran several times higher than memory actually used. Cutting those overheads usually hurt performance, which shows current designs pay dearly for readiness. Simulations extended the findings toward production scale.
arxiv-2509-03304:
Ali Abbas, Sajid Ali, and Ismail Shah developed control charts in 2025 for count data with far too many zeros. Quality control charts watch a process over time and flag when its output drifts out of line. Some count processes also produce excess zeros and wide spread, which a zero-inflated negative binomial model is built to handle.

The authors design both a classic Shewhart chart and an exponentially weighted moving average chart for such data. The second chart weights recent observations more heavily, so it notices small persistent shifts sooner. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations compared the charts by how quickly they signal a change. A real dataset demonstrates practical use. The weighted chart came out ahead of the Shewhart chart overall.
arxiv-2509-03404:
F. D. Arizo-Borillo and 24 co-authors derived galaxy stellar mass functions from a wide optical survey in 2025. A stellar mass function counts how many galaxies exist at each mass, separately here for quiescent galaxies, which have stopped forming stars, and star-forming ones. Their data come from a twelve-band photometric survey covering thousands of square degrees nearby.

About nine hundred thousand galaxies with measured brightness and estimated distances entered the sample. Masses and star formation rates came from fitting each galaxy's light distribution across bands. The resulting functions fit classic Schechter curves and agree with earlier studies. Heavy galaxies were far more likely to be quiescent, and above a high mass threshold nearly all were. A leading galaxy formation model overproduced mid-mass star-forming galaxies by comparison.
arxiv-2509-03504:
I. Grojnowski and one co-author wrote a 2025 mathematics paper on recognising flag varieties and reductive groups from geometric data. Flag varieties are special spaces built from nested subspaces, central in geometry and representation theory. Their starting point is a family of schemes, a general kind of geometric space, equipped with certain fibrations.

From those fibrations they extract simple roots, coroots, and a Cartan matrix, the data that classify such groups. The space is then shown to form a bundle with that flag variety as fibre, for the matching Chevalley group. A uniform recovery of classic isomorphism and isogeny theorems follows. Those theorems say a pinned reductive group is fixed by its root data, and maps between data give unique maps between groups.
arxiv-2509-03804:
Ad-Deen Mahbub and one co-author's 2025 research paper is about estimating buoyancy for autonomous underwater vehicles in real time inside a simulator. Accurate buoyancy matters for believable underwater physics, yet the NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform has no native buoyancy system. External solutions must compute how much of a vehicle sits below the waterline as it moves.

Their approach builds a convex hull from the vehicle's mesh geometry extracted from the simulation. The hull portion crossing the water level along the vertical axis gives the submerged volume, beating traditional geometric approximations in accuracy. A cross-sectional area extension trims the computational cost of repeated updates. Buoyant force then adapts continuously to orientation, depth, and wave motion, with waves swinging a third of a metre. Tests use a vehicle built for the SAUVC 2025 competition. The method runs in real time, scales to other designs, and needs no precomputed hydrodynamic model.
arxiv-2509-04104:
Keara Schaaij and three co-authors study how to capture a person's everyday word choices in a 2025 research paper. People naturally start matching each other's vocabulary during conversation, a habit called lexical alignment. Chat agents that could mirror a user's words might communicate better, but first they need a stable profile of how that user talks. The team varied how much spoken data went into each profile, and how many favorite words it kept per word type.

Ten minutes of transcribed speech proved enough for a compact profile to work best. Small profiles kept five examples for some word types and ten for others. Results offer practical guidance for building agents that adapt to individual speakers over time.
arxiv-2509-04204:
Andrey A Dobrynin and one co-author, Aleksey N Glebov, sort network patterns by how their parts team up in a 2025 mathematics paper. A dominating set in a graph reaches every vertex, meaning every point is in the set or next to one. Two groups form a coalition when neither reaches everything alone but their union does. Splitting all vertices into such groups gives a coalition partition, and a second graph records which groups partner together.

Only subcubic graphs are studied, where no vertex has more than three neighbors and the graph stays connected. The authors characterize every partner graph that can arise from such networks. Results give network designers a complete menu of possible teamwork patterns.
arxiv-2509-04304:
Juraj Vladika and two co-authors test whether large language models keep repeating medical advice that science has left behind in a 2025 research paper. Models learn from fixed training snapshots, while clinical guidance changes as new studies land. Two new question sets probe the risk. One holds over sixteen thousand questions drawn from systematic reviews across biomedicine. The other keeps only questions where expert consensus actually flipped over time.

Eight prominent models answered both sets. Every model leaned on outdated knowledge in the changed-consensus cases. The authors trace the problem to stale pre-training data and training choices, then sketch remedies. Safer medical assistants will need fresher knowledge pipelines, they argue.
arxiv-2509-04804:
Older adults differ widely in how their physical and financial health evolve together. Chitradipa Chakraborty and one co-author model those joint trajectories in a 2025 statistics paper. They propose a Bayesian latent class model for multivariate longitudinal outcomes with excess zeros, where hidden groups share similar outcome patterns over time.

Different outcome types get tailored parts: a Tobit model for medical expenses, a two-part model for debt, and a zero-inflated count model. An adaptive shrinkage method selects variables. Applied to Health and Retirement Study data, the analysis finds several latent clusters, and simulations validate the model's practical usefulness.
arxiv-2509-04904:
Stopping a clinical trial early can distort the final estimate of a treatment's effect. G. Caruso, lead author with three co-authors, propose an information metric for that distortion in a 2025 statistics paper. Group sequential designs allow interim looks and early stopping for benefit or futility, but ignoring those decisions can bias posterior estimates.

Using Kullback-Leibler divergence, a measure of difference between distributions, they quantify distortion across the whole parameter space. Comparing decision boundaries and priors shows how the metric can guide future trial planning. An expected version helps clinicians choose boundaries, adding to standard error-rate control.
arxiv-2509-05004:
Ultrasound scans can flag breast cancer early, and artificial intelligence may help read them more reliably. Mohammad Abbadi, lead author with three co-authors, compare learning methods for breast ultrasound classification in a 2025 study. The aim is early, reliable detection.. They use several public datasets and test classical models alongside deep convolutional networks. Both families are judged on the same scans.

In their experiments, one deep network reaches the highest accuracy and perfect sensitivity for malignant lesions. No malignant case is missed by that model in their tests. Classical models stay competitive when paired with deep feature extraction. That pairing lifts the older methods close to the deep ones. Visual explanations highlight the image regions behind predictions, improving transparency. The authors argue such interpretable systems could support clinical workflows, especially where breast tissue is dense.
arxiv-2509-05404:
Preparing the right starting state can shrink a quantum computation, Thierry N. Kaldenbach and four co-authors show in a 2025 quantum computing paper. In measurement-based computing, the computation runs on a prepared graph state, and tailoring that state to the algorithm can save depth, gates, and even qubits.

The authors improve a simulated annealing search for the best periodic graph states behind repeated rotation patterns, common in simulated physics. They also derive a preparation scheme linking the graph state to how the underlying Hamiltonians fail to commute. Both methods are tested on condensed matter examples and on universal resource states built from minimal generator sets. Comparisons show where each approach wins.
arxiv-2509-05504:
Checking virtual chip prototypes across levels of detail is compared head-to-head by Karl Aaron Rudkowski, Sallar Ahmadi-Pour, and Rolf Drechsler in a 2025 hardware verification paper. Virtual prototypes written in SystemC let engineers analyse designs early, and symbolic execution can explore many behaviours at once.

Two rival tools embody opposite choices: one modifies the SystemC kernel, the other modifies the symbolic execution engine instead. The authors test both on peripherals at different abstraction levels, across verification scenarios and hundreds of planted mutants. The engine-side tool leaves the prototype untouched, while the kernel-side tool runs slightly faster and leaner. Both match older tools limited to one modelling level.
arxiv-2509-05804:
Choosing the right circuit layout for a variational quantum algorithm is the problem addressed by Manish Mallapur and two co-authors in 2025. These algorithms run a tunable quantum circuit and adjust it classically, serving chemistry, optimization, and machine learning tasks. A circuit must reach the needed states yet stay shallow enough to train on today's noisy machines.

Their answer borrows from evolution: candidate circuits mutate and compete, scored by expressibility, a measure of how widely a circuit can reach across possible states. The evolved circuits score high at every target depth while keeping few parameters and shallow depth. Performance matches traditional hand-designed layouts. Because the search ignores the specific problem, one evolved design can be reused across many applications.
arxiv-2509-05904:
Jets plowing through the hot matter of a heavy-ion collision lose energy and spread sideways, and Alois Altenburger and two co-authors study that spreading in a 2025 paper. Their setting is the collision's opening stage, before the matter settles into thermal balance. Standard descriptions lean on a single jet quenching parameter, a summary number for the spreading.

Working inside QCD kinetic theory, the authors extract the full broadening probability, the elastic collision kernel, directly from simulations of those early stages. Small momentum kicks turn out to be more likely than a thermal medium would give, especially along the beam direction. The authors present the extraction as a significant step toward realistic modeling of jet quenching during a collision's first moments.
arxiv-2509-06704:
Claims that rest on human values will be read in unlike ways by unlike people. Amir Homayounirad and four co-authors study how to foresee that split in a 2025 language technology paper. Labeling work usually merges many annotators into one ground truth. That merger hides personal judgment, which matters when the labels concern values.

Two plans are weighed. One infers personal judgment sideways, from value guesses; the other spots it head-on. Spotting it head-on flagged value-laden claims far better. Adding a contrastive loss, which pulls similar cases together and pushes different ones apart, to the standard sorting loss did not raise scores, though it cut reliance on per-label judgment data. The methods help annotation teams spot claims that people may read in unlike ways, backing a more careful labeling process that keeps the split visible instead of averaging it away.
arxiv-2509-06904:
Restoring damaged photos with a small add-on to a big diffusion model is the design of Cem Eteke and three co-authors in a 2025 computer vision paper. Blind restoration must fix unknown degradations. Diffusion methods perform well but usually need auxiliary extractors or heavy fine-tuning of the pretrained model.

Large pretrained diffusion models, the authors observe, keep useful representations even of degraded images. Their BIR-Adapter adds a plug-and-play attention mechanism that trains far fewer parameters, up to thirty-six times fewer than rivals. A sampling guidance step curbs hallucinations, the invented details diffusion models sometimes add. On synthetic and real degradations the adapter matched or beat leading methods in several settings. It also generalized a super-resolution-only model to handle further unknown degradations, showing the add-on approach travels across tasks.
arxiv-2509-07004:
Es-said En-naoui, writing alone in a 2025 mathematics paper, studies restricted sums of Euler's totient function. The totient counts numbers up to a given value that share no common factor with it, and its summatory behavior is a classical topic in analytic number theory. This article extends the author's previous study of those sums.

Two complementary restricted sums are investigated: one over integers coprime to a prime, and one over integers divisible by that prime, which together decompose the full totient sum. Recurrence formulas, congruence relations, and generating function identities are established. A congruence result holds for every prime, and an asymptotic expansion with an error term is derived. The paper also studies average orders and connections with divisor structures, refining understanding of totients in arithmetic progressions.
arxiv-2509-07104:
Cosmic rays on the scale of whole galaxies are reviewed by Philip F. Hopkins in a 2025 overview paper. Cosmic rays are fast charged particles that stream through galaxies and the gas around them. Many researchers now think they shape how stars and galaxies form. The review is written as a teaching guide for readers from several different research fields.

Hopkins explains how models that track cosmic rays together with magnetic fields and moving gas depend on very small scales. He lists common errors in older models, such as simple transport rules and flat, boxed-in test setups. Newer work uses full three-dimensional galaxy models and better transport methods. Combined galaxy and local data now limit how cosmic rays near a billion electron volts move. Open questions close the review.
arxiv-2509-07904:
When two heavy nuclei collide slowly, matter and antimatter can be created, and N. K. Dulaev and 7 co-authors calculate how the nuclei's own magnetic field changes that process in a 2025 physics paper. Electron-positron pairs appear from the strong electric fields between the nuclei. The moving nuclei also generate magnetic interactions, often left out of simpler treatments.

Solving the time-dependent Dirac equation in a rotating frame, the team includes both magnetic effects and rotational coupling. Projecting the results onto free positron states yields energy spectra sorted by emission angle, with and without the magnetic term. Comparing the two shows exactly how much the field shifts pair production, sharpening theory for experiments with the heaviest atoms.
arxiv-2509-09004:
Andrew Bell and 5 co-authors use implicit neural representations to measure heart muscle motion and strain in a 2025 paper. Tagging MRI can track the left ventricle, but automatic quantification remains hard. Strain values describe how much the muscle deforms.

Their method predicts continuous displacement from learned latent codes, with no optimization needed at test time. On hundreds of UK Biobank test cases, it achieves the best tracking accuracy among compared methods. Errors in global circumferential and radial strain are also lowest. It runs about three hundred eighty times faster than the most accurate baseline. The speed suits large heart imaging datasets.
arxiv-2509-09204:
A deepfake detector's headline score can hide the fact that it only ever faced easy fakes and one style of real speech. Chin Yuen Kwok and 4 co-authors propose a fairer test, bona fide cross testing, in a 2025 research paper. Standard evaluations pool many synthesizers into one error rate. Synthesizers with more samples dominate that number, and real speech usually comes from a single clean setting.

Their framework pairs fake speech against nine diverse types of genuine speech. Error rates are aggregated in a balanced way across all pairings. The team benchmarked more than one hundred fifty synthesizers this way. They also released a new dataset to support the method. The result is a more robust and interpretable picture of detector strength. For a security technology, knowing the weak spots is the entire point.
arxiv-2509-09304:
Photons traveling a synthetic dimension built from their own frequencies can feel artificial forces that mimic exotic physics. Shu Yang, Bengy Tsz Tsun Wong, and Yi Yang create non-Abelian electric fields on such a chain in a 2025 research paper. Non-Abelian fields, whose components do not commute, govern the strong and weak forces. Copying them with light has been a central challenge for photonic work.

Their device is a ring resonator, split by polarization and modulated in time. Careful control of phase, rotation, and delay programs the synthetic bands and their spin textures. With coherent detection, they saw Zitterbewegung in the photons: the trembling motion predicted for relativistic particles. They also saw it interfere with Bloch oscillations when both field types were present. The work links synthetic dimensions to gauge theory, with possible uses in frequency-domain computing and comb control.
arxiv-2509-09404:
Tongshun Chen and 5 co-authors introduced a flexible cable-driven robot in 2025 that is designed to notice its own wear. Soft continuum robots bend well in tight, messy places, yet repeated motion can permanently deform parts and weaken them. Judging that fatigue while the robot works has received little attention so far.

Their design splits twisting and bending between two beam types and adds a passive stopper that limits motion safely. Motor torque at the limit pose lets the system estimate stiffness on the spot, with no extra sensors fitted. Tests reported far slower fatigue build-up than a standard design, pointing toward longer, safer operation.
arxiv-2509-09604:
Nisarga Paul and 2 co-authors tackle an inverse problem in 2025: can a quantum system's Hamiltonian be read back from a map of where its states live? Their input is the local density of states near one chosen energy, a quantity experiments can actually measure across a surface.
